title: Why You Remember Inaccurate Details of Emotional Events
hook: Why do we misremember vivid, emotional moments?

narration.text: Highly emotional events often create what feel like perfect memories.
These are called flashbulb memories, vivid and detailed snapshots of a moment.
But despite their clarity, these memories are often surprisingly inaccurate.
Our brains don't record events like a camera or a computer.
Instead, memory is reconstructive, meaning we rebuild it each time we recall it.
We fill in gaps with other information, beliefs, or even new experiences.
This means your memory of a significant event can subtly change over time.
It explains why eyewitness accounts can sometimes differ so much.
Have you ever realised a strong memory was actually different?

description: Discover why our most vivid memories, known as flashbulb memories, are often inaccurate. Learn about reconstructive memory and how our brains rebuild past events, sometimes altering the details.
topic: Why you often remember vivid but inaccurate details of highly emotional events, explaining flashbulb memories and reconstructive memory.
